items.title: Adobe is opening Photoshop to your AI agent
points: Adobe is integrating AI agents deeper into its Creative Cloud suite, letting creators delegate multi-step tasks while retaining full control and editability over projects.

Adobe previewed local MCP (Model Context Protocol, a standard that lets third-party AI agents interact directly with an app's files) integrations for Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects, launching in private beta early 2027.
Creative Agent gets a Plan Mode (lets users review and adjust an agent's proposed workflow before it runs) and a Model Selector (lets users choose which AI model executes a given task).
Always-on background agents will eventually handle recurring tasks without active user direction.
Keeping native project files editable after agent edits matters because AI outputs often need refinement, and pros require precise control for final delivery.

issues.subject: ☕️ Adobe is opening Photoshop to your AI agent

headlines: Adobe is integrating AI agents deeper into its Creative Cloud suite, letting creators delegate multi-step tasks while retaining full control and editability over projects.

The company previewed local MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations that allow third-party AI agents to make changes directly in native Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects files while keeping work editable—launching in private beta early 2027.
Adobe's Creative Agent gets new controls including Plan Mode to review agent workflows and Model Selector to choose which AI models execute tasks, giving creators oversight before agents act.
Always-on background agents will eventually handle recurring tasks without requiring active direction from users.

sections.title: Adobe's Three-Pronged Agent Strategy
points: 1. Multi-step task delegation: Creators can hand off complex, repetitive production work to AI agents while staying in charge of creative direction.
2. Granular control mechanisms: Plan Mode lets users review and adjust the agent's proposed workflow before execution; Model Selector lets them pick which AI engines run specific tasks.

3. Third-party agent compatibility: Upcoming local MCP integrations (available early 2027) will let creatives connect their existing preferred agents to modify native project files without losing editability.

sections.title: Why Editability Matters for Professional Workflows
points: 1. AI-generated outputs frequently need refinement, and keeping native project files editable ensures creators can step in at any point to make precise adjustments without restarting.
2. Adobe's pro-grade tools provide the precision control that production professionals require for final delivery; agents handle bulk work, humans handle detail work.
3. The workflow preserves the creator's authority: you set direction, choose the agent, and retain control over the final creative outcome.
